title: Message/set update has no spec whitelist; server-set field rejection list will drift from jmap-chat-types over time
description:
Site: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/message.rs:514-534 (MESSAGE_READONLY list) + 514 (comment 'MAINTENANCE: when adding a server-set field to Message in jmap-chat-types, add its wire name here too.').

The comment explicitly acknowledges a manual-sync invariant between two crates. Without compile-time enforcement, every future Message field addition in jmap-chat-types creates a window where the new server-set field is patchable from clients until someone remembers to add it here. The same pattern repeats in:
- chat.rs:406 CHAT_READONLY (same comment 'INVARIANT...add new server-set fields here at the same time as adding them to the Chat struct')
- space.rs:898-906 SPACE_READONLY
- ban.rs:220 BAN_READONLY
- emoji.rs:437 EMOJI_READONLY
- position.rs:208 POSITION_READONLY
- contact.rs:156 CONTACT_READONLY
- presence.rs:161 PRESENCE_READONLY

Eight sites, each carrying a hand-maintained list keyed by string. Tests don't fail when the list is wrong; the failure mode is silent client overwrite of a server-set field. Past slips will look identical to deliberate omissions in git blame.

Maintenance consequence: every PR adding a new field to a jmap-chat-types data struct silently breaks server-set protection unless the reviewer remembers to grep for the type name. With 30+ workspace crates and sibling extensions (calendars, contacts, tasks, filenode, sharing, metadata), this becomes an N-way invariant.

Mitigations to consider:
1. Move the readonly list to the type's marker trait (jmap-chat-types::JmapObject or a new ReadOnlyFields trait); the compiler enforces every type names its server-set fields once. Handler reads from the trait.
2. Or: derive the readonly list from a struct-level attribute, generated by a proc macro that lives in jmap-chat-types.
3. Or: tag fields with #[serde(skip_deserializing)] for the *patch* type (separate from the get type). The PatchObject already supports this pattern; the question is whether every server-set field has an opt-out at the patch-deserialize boundary.
close_reason: Landed on main as ef7fbaa8 (fix(chat-server): allowlist Message/set updates). Adversarial review passed at the lane commit. Integration CI all green at 9e113188 (stable+beta 3448 passed).
